nodes.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, where $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is either a node or undefined (at the end of a list), the initial pointer-jumping state gives each node $v$ the pointer $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ and the distance $0$ if $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is undefined and $1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Initial state of pointer jumping

nodes.summary: Given nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ with a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ and values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$, the initial state gives each node $v$ the pointer $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ (undefined at the end of a list) and the sum $x_v$.
nodes.title: Initial state of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. For every node $v$ and every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $k$ steps from $v$ runs off the end of the list if and only if $k > \operatorname{rank}(v)$.
nodes.title: The characteristic property of the rank

nodes.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, where $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ is either a node or undefined, the $k$-step jump from $v$ is the node reached by applying $\mathrm{succ}$ $k$ times starting at $v$, and is undefined if some step is undefined: the $0$-step jump from $v$ is $v$, and the $(k+1)$-step jump is $\mathrm{succ}$ of the $k$-step jump.
nodes.title: Iterated successor

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. Then for every node $v$, entry $v$ of the table returned by list ranking by pointer jumping, which runs $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds, is the rank of $v$.
nodes.title: Pointer jumping ranks every list in ⌈log₂ n⌉ rounds

nodes.summary: For a successor map $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, list ranking by pointer jumping runs $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds of pointer jumping on arrays, starting from the initial state, and returns the resulting array of distances, whose entry $v$ is the distance of node $v$.
nodes.title: List ranking by pointer jumping

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a partial successor function on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ under which every list ends, that is, from every node, the node reached in $n$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ is undefined, and let $x_v$ be values in an additive monoid $M$. Then for every node $v$, entry $v$ of the array of sums computed by $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds of pointer jumping on arrays is the suffix sum of $v$: the sum, in…
nodes.title: Pointer jumping computes all suffix sums in $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds

nodes.summary: Given a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ and values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$, this is the array of sums obtained after $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds (the least $k$ with $n \le 2^k$) of pointer jumping on arrays, starting from the pointers $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ and the sums $x_v$.
nodes.title: Suffix sums by pointer jumping on arrays

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. If following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $a$ steps from a node $v$ reaches the node $u$, then $a \le \operatorname{rank}(v)$ and $\operatorname{rank}(u) = \operatorname{rank}(v) - a$.
nodes.title: Rank decreases along jumps

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate. The rank of a node $v$ is the least $k$ such that following $\mathrm{succ}$ for $k + 1$ steps from $v$ runs off the end of the list, that is, the number of nodes after $v$ in its list.
nodes.title: Rank of a node in a linked list

nodes.summary: In one parallel round, every node $v$ whose pointer is a node $u$ adds the distance of $u$ to its own distance and moves its pointer to the pointer of $u$ (undefined if that of $u$ is); a node whose pointer is undefined keeps its distance and its undefined pointer.
nodes.title: One round of pointer jumping

nodes.summary: Given an array $P$ of pointers (each a node among $0, \dots, n-1$ or undefined) and an array $D$ of natural-number distances, one round returns arrays $P'$ and $D'$ of length $n$ where, for each node $v$, $P'[v]$ is $P[u]$ if $P[v] = u$ and is undefined if $P[v]$ is undefined, and $D'[v] = D[v] + D[u]$ if $P[v] = u$ and $D'[v] = D[v]$ if $P[v]$ is undefined. Entries missing from the input arrays are read as…
nodes.title: One pointer-jumping round on arrays

nodes.summary: Given an array $P$ of pointers (each a node among $0, \dots, n-1$ or undefined) and an array $S$ of sums in an additive monoid $M$, one round returns arrays $P'$ and $S'$ of length $n$ where, for each node $v$: if $P[v]$ is undefined, then $P'[v]$ is undefined and $S'[v] = S[v]$; if $P[v] = u$, then $P'[v] = P[u]$ and $S'[v] = S[v] + S[u]$. A read outside an array gives an undefined pointer or the sum $0$.
nodes.title: One round of pointer jumping on arrays

nodes.summary: Given a state in which each node $v$ has a pointer $p(v)$, either a node or undefined, and a sum $s(v)$ in an additive monoid $M$, one round produces a new state as follows. If $p(v)$ is undefined, the pointer of $v$ stays undefined and its sum stays $s(v)$. If $p(v) = u$, the new pointer of $v$ is $p(u)$ and its new sum is $s(v) + s(u)$, with $s(u)$ added on the right so that list order is kept.
nodes.title: One round of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: For a successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, the pointer-jumping state after $t$ rounds is defined by recursion on $t$: after $0$ rounds it is the initial state of $\mathrm{succ}$, and after $t + 1$ rounds it is one round of pointer jumping applied to the state after $t$ rounds.
nodes.title: The list-ranking state after $t$ rounds

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a partial successor function on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ under which every list ends, that is, from every node, the node reached in $n$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ is undefined, and let $x_v$ be values in an additive monoid $M$. If $t \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfies $n \le 2^t$, then for every node $v$ the sum of $v$ after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping is the suffix sum of $v$: the sum, in list order,…
nodes.title: Pointer-jumping sums are the suffix sums once $n \le 2^t$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a successor map on the nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ whose lists terminate, and let $t$ be a natural number with $n \le 2^t$. Then after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping from the initial state, the distance of every node $v$ is the rank of $v$.
nodes.title: After enough rounds, the distances are the ranks

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ map each of the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ to its successor or to nothing, and suppose the lists terminate: from every node, $n$ steps run off the end. Write $\mathrm{rank}(v)$ for the number of nodes after $v$. Then for every $t \ge 0$ and every node $v$, after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping, the pointer of $v$ is the node $2^t$ steps down the list from $v$ (no node if the list ends before that),…
nodes.title: The invariant of pointer jumping for list ranking

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a partial successor function on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ and $x_v$ values in an additive monoid $M$. For every $t \in \mathbb{N}$ and every node $v$, after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping the pointer of $v$ is the node reached from $v$ in $2^t$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ (undefined if the list ends sooner), and the sum of $v$ is the sum, in list order, of the values of the nodes reached from $v$…
nodes.title: The invariant of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: For a successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ and $t \ge 0$, the arrays after $t$ rounds are a pair of arrays (pointers and distances) defined by recursion on $t$: after $0$ rounds they are the tabulation of the initial state of $\mathrm{succ}$, and after $t + 1$ rounds they are one round on arrays applied to the arrays after $t$ rounds.
nodes.title: List-ranking rounds on arrays

nodes.summary: Given a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ and values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$, the pair of arrays after $0$ rounds stores the pointers $\mathrm{succ}(v)$ and the sums $x_v$, and the pair after $t + 1$ rounds is one round of pointer jumping on arrays applied to the pair after $t$ rounds.
nodes.title: Arrays after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: Given a partial successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$, values $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$ and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, the state after $t$ rounds is obtained from the initial state (pointers $\mathrm{succ}(v)$, sums $x_v$) by applying one round of pointer jumping $t$ times.
nodes.title: State after $t$ rounds of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{succ}$ be a partial successor function on nodes $0, \dots, n-1$ and $x_v$ values in an additive monoid $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ write $S_k(v)$ for the sum, in list order, of the values of the nodes reached from $v$ in $0, 1, \dots, k - 1$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ (a missing node contributes $0$). Then for all $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ and every node $v$, $S_{a+b}(v) = S_a(v) + S_b(u)$ if the node $u$…
nodes.title: Segment sums add up

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function such that, starting from any node, $n$ steps run off the end of its list, and give every node the value $1 \in \mathbb{N}$. Then for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every node $v$, the segment sum of length $k$ from $v$ (the sum of the values of the first $k$ nodes from $v$, fewer at the end of the list) is $\min(k, \operatorname{rank}(v) + 1)$, where…
nodes.title: Segment sums of unit values count nodes

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, and let each node $v$ carry a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$ (not necessarily commutative). For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a node $v$, the segment sum of length $k$ from $v$ is the sum, in list order, of the values of the first $k$ nodes of the list starting at $v$ (fewer if the list ends sooner); for $k = 0$ it is $0$.
nodes.title: Segment sums

nodes.summary: A pointer-jumping state on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ assigns to each node a pointer, which is either a node or empty (once it points past the end of the list), and a distance in $\mathbb{N}$, the distance covered by the pointer.
nodes.title: Pointer-jumping state for list ranking

nodes.summary: For $n$ nodes and a type $M$, a state assigns to each node $v$ a pointer, which is either a node or none (past the end of the list), and an accumulated value in $M$. The accumulated value is meant to be the sum of the node values from $v$ up to, but not including, the pointer's target.
nodes.title: State of pointer jumping for suffix sums

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, each node $u$ carrying a value $x_u$ in an additive monoid $M$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and a node $v$, this is $x_u$ where $u$ is the node $k$ steps after $v$ along its list, and $0$ if the list ends before $k$ steps.
nodes.title: The value $k$ steps ahead

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function such that, starting from any node, $n$ steps run off the end of its list, and let each node $v$ carry a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$. Then for every node $v$, the suffix sum of $v$ is $x_v$ plus the suffix sum of the successor of $v$, or just $x_v$ if $v$ has no successor.
nodes.title: The characteristic property of suffix sums

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function such that, starting from any node, $n$ steps run off the end of its list. If every node has value $1 \in \mathbb{N}$, then the suffix sum of every node $v$ is $\operatorname{rank}(v) + 1$, where $\operatorname{rank}(v)$ is the number of nodes after $v$ in its list.
nodes.title: List ranking is the special case of unit values

nodes.summary: Let $n$ nodes be linked into lists by a partial successor function, each node $v$ carrying a value $x_v$ in an additive monoid $M$. The suffix sum of a node $v$ is the segment sum of length $n$ from $v$: the sum, in list order, of the values of the first $n$ nodes of the list starting at $v$ (fewer if it ends sooner).
nodes.title: Suffix sums

nodes.summary: The tabulation of a pointer-jumping state $s$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ is the pair of arrays of length $n$ whose entries at $v$ are the pointer and the distance of $v$ in $s$.
nodes.title: Tabulating a list-ranking state

nodes.summary: A suffix-sum pointer-jumping state on $n$ nodes is stored as a pair of arrays of length $n$: the array whose entry $v$ is the pointer of node $v$, and the array whose entry $v$ is the accumulated value of node $v$.
nodes.title: Pointer-jumping state as arrays

nodes.summary: A successor function $\mathrm{succ}$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, mapping each node to its successor or to nothing, terminates when from every node $v$ the walk of $n$ steps along $\mathrm{succ}$ runs off the end, that is, there is no node $n$ steps down the list from $v$.
nodes.title: Terminating successor functions

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
